content.text:
I submitted **index 7 (Ag 0.753, V 0.247)** as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent I measured, 21.5 µA. I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Ag fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.753 | 21.5 µA |
| 0 | 0.821 | 20.2 µA |
| 4 | 0.490 | 0.51 µA |

- **Why index 7:** it sits at the Ag₃VO₄ composition, which the stability model places near the convex hull (0.023 eV/atom), and Ag₃VO₄ is a known visible-light photoanode. The band-gap model gave it 0.008 eV, which is implausible (the measured gap is about 2.2 eV), so I ignored that value.
- **Where the peak probably is:** photocurrent drops about 40-fold in the AgVO₃ region (Ag 0.49) and is nearly flat between Ag 0.75 and 0.82. The best composition is therefore likely in the Ag 0.75–0.8 range.
- **What I didn't check:** I never measured index 12 (Ag 0.787), which lies between my two best points, or index 14 (Ag 0.72). Either could beat index 7. I also skipped the V-rich compositions (Ag below 0.45), since photocurrent fell steeply as V increased. That means the best composition in the library is not confirmed.
- **Unused XRD:** without XRD, the phase at each measured point is inferred from composition, not confirmed.
